extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, military procurement officers, MSC managers, and scholars studying OMB Circular A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for applying OMB Circular A-76 to determine whether commercial activities should be performed in‑house or contracted out, with emphasis on cost comparisons, statement of work, quality assurance, and decision/appeal processes as applied to MSC Nucleus Fleet ships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and primary criterion of A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of Circular A-76 is to provide the most efficient operation at the least cost to government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy directs reliance on commercial sources whenever appropriate; procedures compel critical evaluation of current operating procedures and manning level and solicit bids from the private sector. Efficiency and least-cost are the overriding evaluative goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five basic exceptions to contracting out under A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 specifically listed five basic exceptions when commercial or industrial-type functions were eligible to be performed in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five exceptions are: (1) Procurement from commercial sources would disrupt or delay a DOD program; (2) In-house performance is necessary to maintain military training or readiness; (3) A satisfactory commercial source is not available; (4) Products or services are available from other federal agencies; (5) Contract performance is more costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-76 specifies that profit-seeking firms are not appropriate sources of services that are 'inherently governmental in nature'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include judicial functions, law enforcement, conduct of foreign policy, national defense, intelligence and counter-intelligence operations, tax collection, regulation of industry and commerce, and financial administration of government. Such activities are excluded from A-76 contracting-out procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other categories/situations excluded from A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories and situations are excluded from A-76 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: major system acquisitions governed by other OMB circulars, contractor support services (consulting, studies, professional/management support), activities performed outside the United States/territories, products/services obtained from other federal agencies authorized by law, times of declared war or military mobilization, and DOD procurement of research, development, tests, or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 application four-step procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 application in military agencies follows a four step procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) identify activities appropriate for commercial performance; (2) examine each site for special circumstances that would make commercial sources inappropriate there; (3) perform a cost study at each appropriate site; (4) actually perform the task by contractor or in-house under Circular A-76 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost study (management study) stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost study determines if it is more economical to perform the operation in-house or let a contract and consists of four stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stages: (1) detailed preparation of the performance work statement/statement of work (SOW); (2) cost estimation of work performed by government employees; (3) solicitation of bids (usually fixed-price) from commercial contractors; (4) selection of the lowest bid after cost comparison by the competent organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) quality and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOW should establish the government's actual minimum requirements for performing the service and constitute the specifications for the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW must be sufficiently comprehensive, clear, concise and unambiguous; describe all duties, tasks, responsibilities, and frequencies of performance; describe exactly what work is to be done without prescribing how; set standards to which work must conform (same standards for government or contractor). The SOW directly impacts solicitations, cost comparisons, and subsequent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance plan and performance measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality assurance plan is required along with the SOW; quality standards should be objectively measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan sets surveillance requirements and procedures for government quality assurance evaluators, ensures adequate performance, and establishes administrative mechanisms. Compliance is judged by random sampling methods; financial penalties ('deducts') for noncompliance should be addressed in the SOW and charged if standards are not met. If the SOW establishes a minimum acceptable quality level (AQL), the contractor assumes full legal liability for meeting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government cost estimation standards and MEO requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Government in-house estimates must be based on the 'most efficient and cost effective organization for performance' (MEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The activity need not achieve the MEO prior to the cost comparison, but the MEO is the basis for the government estimate. Cost estimation involves management reviews, detailed procedures for material, personnel, overhead, and standard formulas for retirement, insurance, workmen's compensation, etc. The in-house estimate must be reviewed by a qualified independent activity (e.g., Naval Audit Service) — audit normally begins 120 days prior to bid opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and preferred contract pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the SOW is converted to a solicitation, competitive bids are prepared; firm fixed-price contracts are the preferred method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors may use their preferred method to calculate overhead, wages, fringe benefits, profit, etc. Other pricing arrangements or formal advertising may be approved in rare instances. If no contractors bid, work goes directly to government; sealed bids are opened and compared by the contracting officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison decision rules and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for deciding conversion based on comparison of lowest contract price and government cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the lowest contract price is less than 90 percent of the government cost, a pre-award survey is conducted to determine contractor capability and contract may be awarded. If all contract bids exceed 90 percent of in-house cost, government performance is retained. After adjustments, conversion will not occur unless it results in savings of more than 10 percent of the government estimated personnel-related cost (the 10% differential accounts for loss of production, temporary decreases in efficiency, and other risks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison adjustments and differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments made to in-house and contract prices during cost comparison to reflect conversion realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments include: cost of capital charge when government assets are required for contractor performance; conversion costs (one-time switching costs); additional overhead absorption costs when capacity is reduced; deduction of potential federal income tax revenue that would be paid by the contractor. These differentials are applied before final comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey and contractor capability verification
rubrics_metrics.description: If contract price appears sufficiently less costly, a pre-award survey is required to determine if the lowest bidder is capable of performing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pre-award survey verifies contractor responsibility and capability; if satisfactory, contract awarded and in-house operation dismantled. If not, further action or retention of government performance may result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision announcement, public availability, and appeals timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After approval, results of the cost study are announced and detailed analysis made available; limited period for appeals exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no significant discrepancies are identified or an appeal lodged within 5 working days (which contracting officer may extend up to 15 days for complex decisions), the contracting officer will either award the contract or cancel the solicitation. Implementation timelines: if function remains in-house, implementation of the MEO must be initiated within 30 days and completed within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency inventory and annual update requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 requires all executive agencies to develop an inventory of their activities and annually update it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventory is used to determine which activities should remain government functions and which could be performed by commercial contractors; DOD maintains its list centrally (Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Installations) Installation Services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation considerations for specific contexts (e.g., ship operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Context-specific limitations and considerations affect A-76 implementation for MSC ships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from MSC studies: high-tempo battle group operations may be difficult with contract crews; dedicated pools of merchant mariners and no-strike agreements may be necessary to ensure crew continuity under contract operations. Practical operational constraints and mission-readiness concerns must be considered when applying A-76.
